notes: Meta-analytic pooled effect: DCS↔overall health (k=179, 80 studies, N=36823). Random effects r=.147 (.112–.183) p<.001. Converted r→d via d=2r/√(1-r²). SE(d) via delta method from SE(r). I²=83.23. Egger test significant but trim-and-fill found 0 missing studies; no adjustment needed. Cross-sectional=91.1% of findings. Flatter DCS→worse health.

Meta-analytic pooled effect: DCS↔immune/inflammatory outcomes (k=14). Random effects r=.288 (.091–.464) p=.005. LARGEST subgroup effect. Converted r→d. I²>50%. N estimated from typical study sizes. Inflammatory markers include IL-6 CRP TNF-α. Flatter DCS→more inflammation.

Meta-analytic pooled effect: DCS↔depression (k=52, most common outcome). Random effects r=.106 (.047–.165) p<.001. Converted r→d. Depression was 29.1% of all 179 findings. Includes both symptom scales and diagnoses. Flatter DCS→more depression.

Meta-analytic pooled effect: DCS↔fatigue (k=8). Random effects r=.167 (.048–.281) p=.006. Converted r→d. Fatigue accounted for 4.5% of findings. Includes cancer-related fatigue studies (Bower et al 2005). N estimated. Flatter DCS→more fatigue.

Meta-analytic pooled effect: DCS↔anxiety (k=15). Random effects r=-.084 (-.173–.006) p=.066. NOT SIGNIFICANT — CI crosses zero. Only health outcome with negative direction. Converted r→d. Included because anxiety is key CRCI construct; negative d means flatter DCS associated with LESS anxiety (unexpected). N estimated.
